messages:
maria: Heads up — saw NCCL hangs and job failures on g5pool-dal3 during a stress run. GPUs showing intermittent RDMA errors, packet drops between hosts. Anyone on call?
ashok: Link to logs/host?
maria: pastebin: https://redwood.internal/p/abc123 (redacted) — quick snippet below:
```
[2026-03-18T09:12:02Z] nccl: transport error: RETRY_EXCEEDED
[2026-03-18T09:12:03Z] ibv_devinfo: port 1 rx_errors: 148 tx_errors: 0
ethtool -S mlx5_core | grep rx
rx_packets: 1223456 rx_errors: 12345
```
devon: Is this only DAL3 east-west? Any cross-rack pattern?
maria: Only DAL3 so far, racks r-12 -> r-15 mostly. Seen during multi-GPU allreduce ramps.
tina: Could be switch buffer/MTU mismatch or PFC oscillation. Any jumbo changes pushed recently? :thinking_face:
infra-oncall: We rolled kernel 6.6 + mlx5 5.14 on r-13 last night as part of the NIC roll.
devon: Kernel + driver mismatch can cause skb fragmentation or unexpected checksum drops on some firmware versions.
liz: Suggest checking PFC counters and switch port MTU and link-level drops. Also capture `tcpdump -i ib0 -s 1600` and `ibv_devinfo -v`.
maria: Did a short pcap — saw RoCEv2 fragmented packets and retransmits. Hosts show MTU 9000; some switches report 9216 on a few ports. Looks like an MTU mismatch chain.
ashok: MTU mismatch between host and switch = classic fragmentation -> RDMA retransmits. We should sync MTU across path.
ashok: Also check `net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing`? (not RDMA but may matter for fallback).
tina: I'll open a ticket with the switch vendor (Juniper) — need firmware logs.
deploy-bot: Scheduled action suggested: cordon + drain affected nodes (r-13) -> update NIC firmware -> restart mlx driver -> bring back. Estimated downtime per host ~10m.
infra-oncall: Capacity note: draining r-13 will impact queued jobs; DAL3 has ~18% spare GPUs currently. We may hit capacity throttle if we drain > 6 nodes at once.
maria: Operational mitigation while we fix: set environment `NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1` for non-latency-critical jobs to fallback to TCP so GPUs don't sit idle waiting on retries.
devon: Good temporary mitigation. Also add `NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME=eth*` for fallback routing.
liz: Plan of action: 1) Verify full MTU path (hosts, ToR, spine) and align to 9000; 2) Collect switch counters (ifInErrors/ifOutErrors, PFC stats) from r-12..r-15; 3) Schedule NIC firmware/driver rollbacks or update to vendor-recommended combo; 4) Apply rolling reboots with cordon/drain windows to avoid capacity crunch.
ashok: I'll take node draining for r-13 and coordinate slots with SRE schedule.
tina: I'll file vendor ticket + attach PCAP and `ibv_devinfo` dump.
maria: I'm enabling the TCP fallback canary on r-14 now for two low-priority jobs. Will report back in 15m.
infra-oncall: Noted — please post impacts on the runbook page: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/rdma-issues
ashok: FYI — cost note: retries + stalls are causing higher GPU walltime and pushes into higher committed billing; fixing quickly reduces wasted cycles.
maria: Update: canary started, fallback worked, GPUs resumed work. Still seeing occasional rx error spikes.
liz: Once vendor confirms, prefer stable firmware combo rather than patchy MTU workarounds.
maria: Thanks all — keeping this thread updated. I'll ping when we have vendor ETA and schedule. :thumbsup:
